correctness.rationale: For the explicitly labelled degree-five icosahedral graph, all 531,441 ternary configurations were checked by C++17 functional-graph traversal and independent NumPy whole-space iterate arrays. They agree cell by cell on the nine-row entry/period table, every orbit root and basin size, the 200 temporal three-cycles and global F^11=F^8 identity. The explicit code-2824 orbit reaches zero at step eight and not step seven, proving sharpness; 420 states have that maximal delay. A separate Python symmetry checker checks all 120 distinct adjacency-preserving permutations, verifies group closure, uses a proved upper bound 12*10 and obtains exactly seven classes. Direct reproducible source programs, graph input and expected output are supplied; finite enumeration is exhaustive, not extrapolated.

originality.rationale: The joint two-contact icosahedral orbit, entry-time, basin and seven-class statement was compared by implication to exact published one-contact icosahedral records, four-state icosahedral records, multi-contact graph criteria, and relevant 2011/2016/2018 primary literature. No comparison supplies the sharp two-contact functional-map identity or any of its 200 individual attraction basins. The one-contact source explicitly enumerates phase representatives, so its tables can be filtered to recover some of the static wave population; the originality assessment does not rely on that static count in isolation. The independent two-contact transient and basin census, especially the longer worst-case relaxation clock, survives that coverage. Unindexed equivalent work remains a real residual risk.
residual_risks: Full text of the 1993 archive preprint was not materially read; it is used for historical model context, not decisive exclusion.
The one-contact published icosahedral CSV can be filtered to recover some static θ=2 recurrent states; static count and symmetry classes alone are therefore not claimed as independently novel.
A previously unindexed two-contact icosahedral functional-graph computation could reproduce some or all results.
No independent external audit of the exact code and claimed priority has occurred.

value.rationale: The two-contact threshold is the largest below strict majority on the canonical twelve-vertex five-regular icosahedral triangulation. The complete natural dynamics at this boundary show an extreme 242-fold reduction in recurrent wave orbits relative to the published single-contact count, while increasing the sharp entry cutoff from six to eight. Seven residual geometric wave classes and exact basin sizes 3,6,12 are structural and probabilistically interpretable finite invariants useful as a benchmark for nonlinear excitation thresholds. The main contribution is the precise two-contact transient and basin classification, which the known one-contact phase representatives cannot provide. The result is neither an arbitrary graph slice nor a mere renaming of a known theorem.
